name: Patreon membership tiers for an existing audience
summary: Fans pay a monthly (or per-creation) subscription for exclusive posts, early access, downloads or community perks.
howItWorks: Publish a Patreon page with 2-4 tiers and post exclusive content (files, tutorials, early access) on a schedule. Patrons are existing followers of your free work who pay to support you. Without an audience conversion is near zero; typically 1-5% of engaged followers convert.

payout.minimumPayout: Low/none (exact payout minimum not re-confirmed; PayPal payout fee ~1%)
payout.notes: Current standard plan: 10% platform fee plus payment processing, currency conversion and payout fees (patreon.com/pricing). Pages launched before Aug 2025 may keep legacy 5-12% plans. Payout minimums/fees per method could not be re-fetched (help center blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere in the reference set; income taxable.

availability.notes: Payouts via PayPal/Payoneer in most countries; Stripe deposit where supported.

automationPlan: AI-draft exclusive posts from public work
manualSteps: Build the audience that feeds the page
Make the core creative work patrons pay for
evidence: Patreon has paid creators billions since 2013; many creators earn $1k-$100k+/mo, but the median page earns little.

tools: Patreon (free to start; 10% fee on standard plan)
AI for drafting posts and perks
skills: converting an existing audience into members

unitEconomics.notes: Common tiers $3-$10; 10% platform fee plus payment processing (~5-8% on small pledges) gives ~18% total.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Patreon rewards creators who already have an engaged audience (YouTube, podcasts, webcomics); typical conversion is ~1-5% of active fans. New creators without traffic rarely get past a handful of patrons. The 2025 move to a single 10% plan raised fees for new pages, and Apple in-app pricing changes added friction.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch with a low $3-$5 tier plus one higher tier with tangible perks; raise prices for new patrons and add annual billing once churn stabilises.
profitPath: Month 0: set up page and 2-3 tiers (cost $0)
Month 1-2: announce to existing audience; first 5-20 patrons
Month 3-6: regular exclusive posts, reduce churn
Month 6-12: $30-$300/month for creators with 5k+ engaged followers

name: Tip jar and lightweight memberships on Ko-fi / Buy Me a Coffee
summary: One-off tips plus optional monthly memberships, commissions and a small shop, paid directly into your PayPal/Stripe.
howItWorks: Create a Ko-fi or Buy Me a Coffee page and link it from READMEs, videos, blogs and bios. Readers tip $3-$10 or subscribe monthly. Ko-fi takes 0% on donations (5% on memberships/shop unless Gold) and pays into your PayPal/Stripe; Buy Me a Coffee takes 5% (no monthly fee) and pays out to your bank via Stripe/Wise in 44 countries.

methods: Buy Me a Coffee: Stripe/Wise -> bank
payout.minimumPayout: $0 platform minimum (Ko-fi pays straight to PayPal/Stripe; BMC states none)
payout.frequency: instant per transaction; Stripe/PayPal withdrawal schedule
payout.notes: BMC: 5% transaction fee, creators keep 95%, payouts via Stripe and Wise in 44 countries (buymeacoffee.com/faq). Processor ~3% + $0.30 on top. Ko-fi fee terms not re-fetched this run (help center blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Voluntary tips are legal in all reference countries; taxable income.

availability.notes: Ko-fi works wherever PayPal can receive or Stripe operates; PayPal receiving is unavailable or restricted in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Lebanon, Libya, Iraq). BMC pays out in 44 countries via Stripe/Wise.

automationPlan: Template tip links into all READMEs/posts
manualSteps: Produce the free content that motivates tips
evidence: Ko-fi's help center documents 0% fees on donations and direct-to-PayPal/Stripe payments; many open-source maintainers and artists publicly show Ko-fi supporters.

tools: Ko-fi (free, 0% on donations) or Buy Me a Coffee (5% fee)
skills: producing work people want to thank you for (open source, art, guides)

unitEconomics.notes: Most tips are $3-$5; processor ~3% + $0.30 plus 0% (Ko-fi donations) or 5% (Buy Me a Coffee) platform fee gives ~12% on a $5 tip.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Tips flow to people with visible, useful free work and a clear ask; most pages receive nothing without an audience. Zero cost makes any tip pure profit, but amounts stay small. Failure mode: no traffic to the page. Verifier: likelihood lowered from 25 to 10 to sit below Patreon (15), since tips convert less often than memberships and most pages get nothing.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Set a default 'coffee' unit ($3-$5) and add a monthly membership or small digital shop for higher-value supporters.
profitPath: Month 0: create page, add link to README/bio (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first tips if audience exists ($5-$30)
Month 3-6: add memberships/commissions
Month 6-12: $10-$100/month for active creators

name: Paid Discord/Telegram or Skool community (Whop, LaunchPass, Skool)
summary: Charge a monthly fee for access to a gated chat community or Skool group around a niche skill or interest.
howItWorks: Run a focused community (interview prep, niche hobby, language practice) where members pay monthly for access, resources and your presence. Whop/LaunchPass bill via Stripe and auto-grant Discord/Telegram roles; Skool bundles forum, courses and gamification. Trading/betting 'signals' groups are excluded.

methods: Whop payouts (bank, PayPal, Coinbase; options vary by country)
payout.minimumPayout: Whop: $10 minimum withdrawal; Stripe-based tools: Stripe default
payout.notes: Whop processing 2.7% + $0.30 (+1.5% intl cards, +1% FX); payout fees: next-day ACH $2.50, wire $23, instant 4% + $2.50 (Whop's separate platform fee, ~3%, not re-confirmed). LaunchPass Premium $29/mo + 3.5% + Stripe (free tier $0/mo). Skool Hobby $9/mo + 10% or Pro $99/mo + 2.9%.

legality.notes: Legal; avoid unlicensed financial signals/gambling. Auto-renewal/cancellation laws apply.

availability.notes: Whop pays out to 200+ countries (excluding sanctioned/restricted ones) via bank, PayPal or Coinbase; Skool/LaunchPass rely on Stripe and only pay out in Stripe countries (~35-40% of reference list).

manualSteps: Seed initial members and be personally present
evidence: Skool's public leaderboard shows communities with thousands of paying members; Whop, Skool and LaunchPass publish official fee and payout docs. Availability raised to 75 because Whop's payout docs list 200+ countries.

tools: Whop (processing 2.7% + $0.30, no platform fee) or LaunchPass ($29/mo) or Skool ($9-$99/mo)
skills: audience building; AI helps with content and moderation

unitEconomics.notes: Niche paid communities commonly $10-$50/month; Whop charges no separate platform fee, only processing 2.7% + $0.30 (+1.5% international cards), ~5% on a $20 membership.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost on Whop + Discord; Skool/LaunchPass add $9-$99/month.

marketConditions.notes: Creators with an audience in high-value niches (trading education, career skills, AI tooling) monetise via Skool/Whop; Skool's marketing push in 2024-2026 brought many copycat communities and buyer fatigue. Without an existing audience, member acquisition is the bottleneck, and churn of 10-20%/month is normal. Verifier: Whop fee corrected from ~10% to ~5% (docs.whop.com/fees); median month-12 net lowered from $120 to $60 to agree with a 15% chance of reaching $100/month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch a founding-member price (~50% off) for the first 20-50 members, then raise the price for new members as content and testimonials accumulate.
profitPath: Month 0: set up Discord + Whop and a clear promise (cost $0)
Month 1-2: founding members from your audience; expected $50-$300
Month 3-6: weekly events, testimonials, raise price
Month 6-12: $100-$1,000/month for niches with demand

name: Membership site with gated content (Ghost, Memberful)
summary: Own-domain site where paying members unlock articles, videos, downloads and a members-only area.
howItWorks: Run an own-domain site on Ghost or WordPress + Memberful where premium posts, archives, templates or videos require a paid Stripe membership. You own the domain and email list. Ghost takes 0% of revenue (Ghost(Pro) Publisher $29/mo billed yearly, or self-host on a cheap VPS); Memberful Standard charges $49/mo plus 4.9%.

payout.notes: Ghost: no Ghost transaction fee, Stripe fees apply; paid subscriptions need Ghost(Pro) Publisher ($29/mo yearly; Starter $18 excludes them) or self-hosting. Memberful Standard $49/mo + 4.9%.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; digital VAT/GST rules apply in EU/UK/AU.

availability.notes: Requires Stripe in your country (~35-40% of the reference list); otherwise use Patreon/Whop instead.

automationPlan: AI-assisted drafting and SEO of free posts that funnel to paid
risks: Slow audience growth without an existing following
evidence: Ghost publishes that its creators collectively earn tens of millions per year (e.g. 404 Media, Platformer run on Ghost memberships).

tools: Ghost(Pro) Publisher ($29/mo billed yearly) or self-hosted Ghost (~$6/mo VPS)

unitEconomics.notes: Typical memberships $5-$10/month; Ghost takes 0%, Stripe ~2.9% + $0.30 (~7% on $8).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = Ghost(Pro) Publisher ($29/month); self-hosting cuts it to ~$6.

marketConditions.notes: Independent publishers with a niche expertise and an email list (often from social media) succeed; generic content competes with free AI answers. Subscription fatigue rose in 2025-2026. Most new sites never cover the hosting fee.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a free tier to build the list and a $5-$8 paid tier; add annual plans (2 months free) and raise prices once open rates and retention are strong.
profitPath: Month 0: launch Ghost site with free newsletter ($10 + $29/mo)
Month 1-6: grow free list to 1,000+
Month 6-9: open paid tier; 2-5% of list converts
Month 9-12: $50-$300/month for disciplined publishers

name: 1-to-1 online tutoring on Preply, italki or Wyzant
summary: Teach languages or academic subjects over video to students the marketplace sends you, at your own hourly rate.
howItWorks: Create a tutor profile with intro video and set an hourly rate. Students find you via search, book a trial, then buy packages. Preply keeps the trial and 18-33% after; italki ~15%; Wyzant (US) 25%. Strongest demand: English, native languages, exam prep, math.

payout.notes: italki minimum withdrawal $30; Payoneer flat $3. Wyzant pays to US bank accounts only. Commission and withdrawal figures for Preply/italki/Wyzant could not be re-fetched this run (help centers block automated access); treat as approximate.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; contractor income. Wyzant tutors must be US residents.

availability.notes: Preply and italki accept tutors from most countries and pay via Payoneer/PayPal/Wise; Wyzant is US-only.

automationPlan: AI-generated lesson plans, homework and level tests
AI feedback on student writing before lessons
fullCycle: Apply as tutor and pass verification
evidence: Preply and italki each host tens of thousands of active tutors; Wyzant support docs specify tutors keep 75% of their rate.

unitEconomics.notes: Median marketplace rates ~$15-$30/hour; commission ~15% (italki) to 18-33% (Preply, plus 100% of trial lessons) and 25% (Wyzant). Hours include prep. Commissions are estimated (Preply, italki and Wyzant help pages bot-blocked).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Tutors with niche specialisms (exam prep, business English, rare languages) and strong reviews fill calendars; generalists compete with thousands of low-priced tutors. AI conversation tools (ChatGPT voice, Duolingo Max) reduced demand for casual practice in 2025-2026. Failure modes: no trial conversions early, trial lessons paid at 0% on Preply.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start 20-30% below comparable tutors to win first reviews, then raise rates for new students every 10-20 reviews.
profitPath: Month 0: create profile with intro video (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first trial lessons and regular students; expected $100-$300
Month 3-6: 10-15 hours/week, raise rates
Month 6-12: $400-$1,000/month net

name: On-demand English conversation tutoring on Cambly
summary: Platform-set per-minute pay for chatting with English learners whenever you go online; no lesson prep required.
howItWorks: Cambly connects English learners to tutors for on-demand or scheduled conversation calls. You are paid a fixed $0.17/minute ($10.20/hour), or $0.20/minute for Cambly Kids, only for minutes actually spent in calls. Students pay Cambly a subscription; you do not set prices or market yourself. Fluency in English is the main requirement; native-speaker preference varies.

payout.minimumPayout: No platform minimum stated on official tutor page
payout.notes: Official tutor page: $0.17/min ($10.20/h), Cambly Kids $0.20/min ($12/h), weekly pay via direct deposit 'and more'.

availability.notes: Open to fluent English speakers globally, but Cambly's official tutor page says it is 'temporarily limiting the number of new tutors' and processing may be slower.

automationPlan: AI conversation topic lists and vocabulary sheets
manualSteps: Every minute of tutoring is live human work
evidence: Cambly's official tutor page lists $0.17/min and $0.20/min (Kids) and weekly direct-deposit pay. paymentProbability lowered 6->5 because the same page says new-tutor intake is currently limited.

unitEconomics.notes: Official pay $0.17/min ($10.20/hour) adult, $0.20/min ($12/hour) Cambly Kids; platform cut is already deducted.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Pay is certain per minute once accepted, but tutor supply is high and waiting online unpaid is common. AI English conversation partners reduce demand. Works best as filler income in low-cost countries or for tutors with scheduled regular students. Cross-catalog calibration: profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 55 to 50 to match esl-company-tutoring and tutoring-marketplaces (same declining/saturated ESL market) given paymentProbability 5 and long unpaid waiting.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you; maximise paid minutes by keeping priority hours and building regular students.
profitPath: Month 0: apply and pass review (cost $0)
Month 1: first calls; expected $50-$150
Month 2-6: priority hours and regular students
Month 6-12: $200-$400/month at 5-10 hours/week

name: Live cohort-based courses on Maven
summary: Teach a multi-week live course to a cohort of paying students; Maven provides storefront, payments and discovery.
howItWorks: You design a 2-6 week live course or a short workshop on a professional skill (e.g. product management, applied AI, data engineering) and list it on Maven. Students (often reimbursed by employers) pay $200-$2,000 per seat. Maven keeps 10% as platform fee (Stripe fees on top) and may promote strong courses in its marketplace. You teach live over Zoom with assignments and peer discussion; recordings can be re-sold as later cohorts.

payout.frequency: after cohort payments clear / Stripe schedule
payout.notes: Maven keeps 10% of each paid enrollment; Stripe fees come out first (e.g. $1,000 -> ~$873.60 to you). Payout schedule set in your Stripe account; Stripe-supported country required.

legality.notes: Education services are legal everywhere; avoid regulated topics (licensed financial/medical advice).

availability.notes: Maven pays via Stripe Connect, limiting instructors to Stripe-supported countries.

automationPlan: Automated reminders, recordings and feedback forms
evidence: Maven's help center states the 10% platform fee and Stripe Connect payouts; Maven (a16z-backed) publicizes instructors earning six figures per cohort.

accounts: Stripe + KYC in a supported country

unitEconomics.notes: Maven cohorts commonly $300-$1,500; Maven 10% plus Stripe (~$1,000 -> $873.60 to you, ~13%). Hours = cohort prep and teaching per student for ~15 students.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = Zoom Pro.

marketConditions.notes: Instructors with an existing professional audience (LinkedIn, newsletter) fill cohorts; Maven's discovery rarely fills a newcomer's first cohort. Free AI tutoring and cheap recorded courses pressure prices, while live accountability still sells to companies with L&D budgets. Verifier: median month-12 net lowered from $700 to $0 because only ~12% of starters fill a paid cohort in their first year; Maven 10% + Stripe confirmed.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Run a beta cohort at ~50% off for testimonials, then raise to market price and add company/team pricing.
profitPath: Month 0: design curriculum and Maven page (cost $15/mo)
Month 1-3: pre-sell beta cohort of 5-15 students
Month 3-6: teach, gather testimonials, raise price
Month 6-12: one cohort per quarter, $500-$3,000/month averaged

name: Paid one-off webinars and live workshops (Luma/Zoom + Stripe)
summary: Sell tickets to 60-180 minute live workshops on a practical topic, then sell the recording.
howItWorks: You pick a narrowly useful topic (e.g. 'Automate your invoicing with n8n', 'Résumé review for junior devs'), create a ticketed event on Luma, Eventbrite or a Stripe payment link, and run it on Zoom/Google Meet. Attendees pay $10-$100 per seat. Luma's free plan takes 5% plus Stripe fees (0% on Luma Plus). Recordings are later sold as an on-demand product.

payout.notes: Luma: 5% platform fee on free plan, 0% on Luma Plus ($59/mo billed annually); Stripe ~2.9% + $0.30 on top.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; consumer refund rules apply to ticket sales.
complianceRequirements: sales tax/VAT on digital services where applicable

availability.notes: Luma and Stripe payouts limited to Stripe countries; Eventbrite payouts cover more countries.

automationPlan: AI-generated slides, worksheets and promo copy
Auto-created event pages and reminder emails
Auto-transcribe/edit recordings into a paid replay
evidence: Luma's help center documents paid events with direct Stripe payouts used by many tech community organisers.

skills: promoting events on social media or newsletter

unitEconomics.notes: Practical workshops sell at $20-$100; Luma free plan 5% + Stripe ~2.9% + $0.30 (~9% on $49). Hours = prep and delivery per attendee at ~10-20 attendees.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = Zoom Pro (free alternatives exist).

marketConditions.notes: Workshops convert when the host already has an audience and a concrete outcome (e.g. a tool tutorial); generic webinars lost value as free AI tutorials and YouTube content grew. Recordings resold as products extend revenue. Most first events sell only a few tickets. Verifier: median month-12 net lowered from $150 to $40 to agree with a 20% chance of reaching $100/month; Luma free-plan 5% fee confirmed.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $20-$30 with early-bird discounts, then raise to $50-$100 and sell recordings and bundles.
profitPath: Month 0: plan one workshop and landing page (cost $15/mo)
Month 1: first event with 5-15 attendees; expected $100-$400
Month 2-6: monthly events, sell recordings

name: Paid mentorship subscriptions on MentorCruise
summary: Mentees pay a monthly fee for ongoing career/technical mentorship (chat + calls) via a curated marketplace.
howItWorks: You apply as a mentor (typically software, design, data, product or career experience) and publish monthly plans, e.g. $150/month for async chat plus 2 calls. Mentees discover you via MentorCruise search and pay a subscription; MentorCruise adds a ~20% markup on top (min $20, capped at $100 for $100-$800 plans; one-off sessions carry a $9-$39 flat fee). Example: $100 plan -> mentee pays $120, mentor gets $100 minus card fees (~$96.40). Payouts via Stripe Connect or bank transfer.

payout.frequency: Stripe: usually within 7 days; bank transfer: monthly (~4th, for prior month)

availability.notes: Stripe Connect where available; direct bank transfer for other countries.

evidence: MentorCruise's help center documents payout mechanics with worked fee examples.

unitEconomics.notes: Mentee-paid plans commonly $100-$300/month; MentorCruise adds its fee on top of the mentor price (a $100 plan is shown as $120) for a ~16.6% average take rate, $20/month minimum, capped at $100 for $100-$800 plans.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Mentors with recognisable employers or niche skills (FAANG, staff engineers, product leaders) attract mentees; generic profiles wait months. Tech layoffs in 2023-2025 increased both demand and mentor supply. AI coaching tools pressure entry-level demand. Verifier: fee corrected from ~23% to ~17% (MentorCruise help page); median month-12 net lowered from $220 to $60 to agree with a 25% chance of reaching $100/month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start below comparable mentors to get first reviews, then raise as your waitlist grows.
profitPath: Month 0: apply and build profile (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first mentee; expected $100-$200
Month 3-6: 2-4 mentees, collect reviews
Month 6-12: $200-$800/month net

name: Per-minute expert phone calls on Clarity.fm
summary: Founders and professionals book short paid calls with you at a per-minute rate you set.
howItWorks: You list your expertise (marketing, fundraising, SaaS, engineering) on Clarity.fm and set an hourly rate that is displayed per minute. Callers are billed per minute; Clarity keeps 15%. Bookings come from Clarity search and, more often, from links you place on your site or social profiles.

payout.minimumPayout: No stated minimum (manual export to PayPal)

legality.notes: Consulting is legal; regulated advice (legal/medical/investment) needs licensing.

availability.notes: Pays via PayPal only, so limited where PayPal cannot receive.

automationPlan: Auto-generated call summaries and follow-up notes
Embed booking widget in content automatically
evidence: Clarity.fm's official expert page (still live, accepting expert applications via LinkedIn) states the 15% fee and PayPal payouts every 15 days; marketplace activity level is unclear.

skills: recognisable expertise founders will pay for

unitEconomics.notes: Experts set $1-$10/minute; Clarity keeps 15% plus PayPal fees (~3%).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Clarity traffic is far below its 2010s peak, so calls come mostly from experts' own audiences. AI assistants now answer many quick founder questions. Profit is near-certain per call but bookings are rare.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start at $1-$2/minute to earn reviews, then raise as your profile ranks.
profitPath: Month 0: create profile (cost $0)
Month 1-6: share the booking link with your audience; first calls rare
Month 6-12: a few calls a month for experts with visibility

name: Sell study notes and exam prep on Stuvia / Docsity
summary: Upload your own original lecture notes, summaries and practice questions; earn per download.
howItWorks: Students and professionals upload original study notes, summaries and exam-prep guides. Buyers searching for a course or exam pay per document; Stuvia takes a per-sale commission (shown when you set the price; reviews put it near 30%) and lets you withdraw once your wallet reaches EUR/USD/GBP 10. Docsity uses a points system convertible to cash. Only sell notes you wrote; reproducing textbooks, professors' slides or exam papers violates copyright and university rules.

payout.frequency: Stuvia: requests before Sunday 23:59 CET processed the following Monday
payout.notes: Stuvia: arrives 2-4 business days after Monday processing (1-2 in South Africa); payout via Tipalti. Exact commission not published (~30% per reviews). Docsity points/payout rules not re-verified (site blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Selling your own notes is legal; some universities prohibit selling notes from their lectures.

availability.notes: Stuvia and Docsity accept sellers internationally; bank payout.

automationPlan: AI-structured summaries from your own notes
evidence: Stuvia's help center documents the 10-unit minimum and weekly Monday payout processing; reviews report average earnings per sale of $4-9.

tools: AI for formatting and practice questions

unitEconomics.notes: Notes sell for ~EUR/USD 5-15; Stuvia only says it takes "a small commission per sale" and shows earnings at pricing time, so ~30% is estimated from reviews. Hours = writing time spread over expected sales.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: Best sellers cover large first-year courses at big universities (NL, UK, ZA) with exam-season peaks. Students increasingly ask AI for summaries, lowering demand for generic notes. Sales are seasonal and concentrated. Verifier: likelihood lowered from 25 to 12 because $100/month needs ~15 sales a month year-round, which few sellers sustain outside exam peaks.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price slightly below the course's top-rated notes, bundle multiple modules, and raise prices before exam season.
profitPath: Month 0: upload notes for 3-5 courses (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first sales around exams
Month 3-6: add bundles and practice exams
Month 6-12: $20-$100/month averaged, peaking at exams

name: Crowdfunding a creative/digital project (Kickstarter, Indiegogo)
summary: Pre-sell a digital game, book, tool or course to backers who pledge for digital rewards.
howItWorks: You build a campaign page with a video, reward tiers (digital copies, early access, credits) and a funding goal. Backers pledge; on Kickstarter you only collect if the goal is met (5% platform fee + 3-5% processing). Indiegogo allows flexible funding. Digital rewards avoid shipping costs.

methods: direct deposit to bank (Kickstarter via Stripe)
payout.notes: Kickstarter: 5% of funds + Stripe ~3-5%, only if funded. Payout starts 14 days after campaign ends and lands 3-14 business days later.

legality.notes: Reward-based crowdfunding is legal; equity crowdfunding excluded. Must deliver promised rewards.

availability.notes: Kickstarter creators must reside in one of 25 countries (AU, AT, BE, CA, DK, FR, DE, GR, HK, IE, IT, JP, LU, MX, NL, NZ, NO, PL, SG, SI, ES, SE, CH, UK, US) with local ID and bank account: only 10 of the ~50 reference countries. Indiegogo accepts more countries (not re-verified).

automationPlan: AI-drafted campaign copy and update posts
Automated backer surveys and digital reward delivery
evidence: Kickstarter has raised billions for creative projects; fee structure documented in help center.

tools: pre-launch page and email list tools (free tiers)
AI for video scripts and art
accounts: Kickstarter account in an eligible country + Stripe

unitEconomics.notes: Median pledge ~$30-$50; Kickstarter 5% + processing 3-5%; cost = digital reward delivery plus pre-launch ads per backer (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; revenue arrives as one lump sum ~2-4 weeks after a successful campaign.

marketConditions.notes: About 4 in 10 Kickstarter projects reach their goal, but first-timers without a pre-launch email list mostly fail, and funded projects often spend the money on delivery. Games and tabletop dominate; AI-generated art is controversial with backers.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Set a low funding goal you can deliver on, offer early-bird tiers 20-30% off retail, and add higher tiers with collectible extras.
profitPath: Month 0-2: build prototype and pre-launch list of 500+ (cost $0-$500)
Month 3: run 30-day campaign
Month 4: receive funds (if funded)
Month 4-12: deliver rewards; sell post-campaign via late pledges

name: Apply for open-source and creator grants/fellowships (FLOSS/fund, NLnet, Sovereign Tech, Emergent Ventures)
summary: Write short applications to foundations that pay maintainers and talented individuals to build public-good work.
howItWorks: Funders award non-dilutive grants for open-source maintenance or ambitious individual projects. FLOSS/fund (Zerodha, up to $1M/yr) gives $10k-$100k per project per year to established projects that publish a funding.json manifest, reviewed quarterly; NLnet gives EUR 5k-50k first grants via recurring calls (Restack, CodeSupply open with a 3 Nov 2026 deadline) to projects with a strong European dimension; Sovereign Tech Agency funds critical OSS infrastructure globally (Fund minimum EUR 50k of work) plus Fellowship/Standards programs; Emergent Ventures offers micro-grants. Payment is by bank transfer after selection and contracting.

payout.notes: STA contracts follow a compliance review of up to 8 weeks; FLOSS/fund requires tax-residency paperwork before disbursing. Emergent Ventures terms not re-verified (site blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Receiving grants is legal; may be subject to sanctions screening.

availability.notes: FLOSS/fund and Sovereign Tech Fund invest globally; NLnet's EU-funded calls require a strong European dimension (applicants usually from Horizon Europe-eligible countries); Emergent Ventures historically global.

automationPlan: AI-assisted research of calls and budget drafting (NLnet requires the proposal itself to be human-written)
evidence: FLOSS/fund allocated $1M in 2025 to projects like Blender, FFmpeg, KDE; NLnet and Sovereign Tech Agency publish open calls and funded-project lists.

accounts: bank account able to receive EUR/USD wires

unitEconomics.notes: NLnet awards ~EUR 5k-50k, FLOSS/fund $10k-$100k, Emergent Ventures $1k-$50k; hours = application effort per award at ~10-20% success (estimate). Grant money pays for the work you then must deliver.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; grants pay in milestones over months.

marketConditions.notes: Funders favour maintainers with existing adoption and credible plans; AI-assisted applications increased volume in 2025-2026, lowering acceptance rates. Grant money is compensation for deliverables, so true profit is modest. Most applicants receive nothing in a given year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Budget at your real hourly rate for clearly scoped milestones; start with small asks to build a funding track record.
profitPath: Month 0: identify 3-5 matching programmes, draft proposals (cost $0)
Month 1-4: submit and wait for review
Month 4-9: first award (if any) and first milestone payment
Month 9-12: deliver and reapply with track record
